When a release cut's tag is not pushed, every install pin on main names a tag that exists on origin.
When a release tag is pushed, the install pins on main name that tag.
payload.description:
## Context
When a release is cut but its tag is not pushed, I want the install pins on main to keep naming a published tag, so nobody who installs from the README or the site gets a missing tag.

## Finding
2026-11-17: basicly release 0.46.2 made version commit 8a0bc4a8, which rewrote the install pins (README.md, site/index.html, .scripts/bootstrap.sh, .scripts/bootstrap.ps1, docs) from v0.46.1 to v0.46.2. The release-process rule pushes main first and the tag only after green CI on the version commit. Quality-gates 43965947002 on 8a0bc4a8 failed, so v0.46.2 was never pushed and was deleted locally. Main and the Pages site (deployed 2026-11-16 22:01 UTC) therefore named a tag that does not exist, and an install from them fails until a later release publishes.

## Fix
Options: push the version commit and tag together only after CI on a candidate; or keep pins on the published tag until the tag push succeeds. Not claimed.
payload.title: Keep install pins on main pointing at a published tag when a release cut stops before the tag push

payload.text: [2026-11-17, Orchestrator] Required check: the release gate refuses a commit that moves install pins to a version whose tag does not exist on the remote. Decision: no separate pin revert now; 0.46.3 rewrites the pins. If 0.46.3 is not published by 23:30 UTC on 2026-11-17, the Orchestrator puts a pin revert to v0.46.1 before the owner as a deploy.

[merged from basicly-jr0l.28, triage 2026-11-17] Record retro proposals machine-locally without ever injecting them
Acceptance carried over:
## Trigger

When a retro proposal is not yet promoted to the shared catalog, I want it recorded in a git-ignored machine-local inbox that no agent reads, so I can keep a finding from being lost without letting it silently shape a session.

## Context

Plan §7.4, resolved by owner decision 2026-07-26. The decision is made; this bead implements it.

DECIDED: record but never inject. A machine-local file collects retro proposals and is never loaded into any agents context. It is an inbox for a human to review, not guidance.

This is the rung between dropping a retro proposal and asking a human to amend the shared catalog, and the shape was chosen to make the named risk structurally impossible rather than merely bounded. The risk in the plan is bypass by accretion - guidance that shapes a machines sessions while never being reviewed - which is a near neighbour of the recorded non-goal of an agent-writable catalog, where a bad implementation bounces off a gate but a bad fragment is absorbed and silently degrades every later lane. An expiring lane that did shape sessions was considered and rejected on that ground: expiry bounds the exposure without removing it.

So the value kept is that a finding is not lost between sessions. The value deliberately not taken is that it never influences behaviour until a human has promoted it through the normal catalog path and its gates.

## Notes

The file must be git-ignored, and it must not live anywhere a projection or a hook would pick it up as guidance - the whole guarantee is that no agent reads it. Assert that rather than assuming it: a test that the path is absent from every projected output and from every always-on file is what makes the claim checkable.

## Scope

payload.description:
## Context
The rules that govern an orchestrator session and the sessions it directs must travel with the repository, not live in one machine's notes. They become catalog fragments, the orchestrator agent source and an orchestration skill, each with its enforcement: orch commands, hooks and doctor checks. Workers get the worker-side fragments; only the orchestrator agent gets the orchestrator side. One fragment lists the three classes: ask-first items the orchestrator decides, owner items the person may approve through the orchestrator, and items that stay in the worker's own window. The CI time check is basicly-jxzin95 and is not built here.
